quest.title: Immernachtreich Apokalypse
quest.description: Fischl has not returned, so the party decides to explore the island first and confirm whether there is a mirage as the divination result indicated and to whom it belongs. Soon, everyone finds a night raven statue, along with a mysterious book that it has brought here — Hymn of the Holy Land. After touching the book, you and the others enter the mirage within...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you awake?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ugh... It's morning again...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's up? Has something happened?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It might sound hard to believe, but no. Nothing's happened.

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: You're awake? Then let's bring you up to speed: We've searched everywhere, and found nothing unusual at all.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Based on the previous two mirages, we should have been able to find something that acts as an entrance.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's weird.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Is it possible that the time has not come yet?

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: You mean, we should wait a little longer?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Yes. Plus, Fischl is still nowhere to be found, and I highly suspect that she's even more eager to find the entrance than we are.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: So let's wait. Let's give the mirage... no, give Fischl some more time.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everyone agrees with Mona and takes a break. Then, they continue the search in two groups.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After numerous round trips with little success, something finally appears on the beach.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's something on the beach!

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: A book? And next to it is... hmm... a raven statue?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This statue looks a lot like Oz...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Why did these two items appear together? Did the raven bring the book here?

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: What's the book about? Is it a diary?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Let's see... "Hymn of the Holy Land"? I've never heard of a book by that title.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: From the cover, it looks like... it was written by Fischl herself?

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: That would certainly fit her personality. "Hymn of the Holy Land"... interesting, I like it.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: As a title, it has a sacred ring to it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what should we do? Should we touch it?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: ...Fischl's still not back.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Never mind, let's head inside first. Once Fischl finds the book, I'm sure she'll be able to catch up with us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon agrees! It's like we're peeping into her diary, so Paimon's sure she'll wanna come in and stop us.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: "Though this truth has long faded from popular memory, scholars have long known that Prinzessin Fischl von Luftschloss Narfidort first descended upon the world during the Time of Chaos, roughly six hundred years before the Era of the Saints."

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: What? A narrator?

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: We really are inside a book, huh. There's even a narrator telling us the story.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, the path has been cut off. We can't go across.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: There's a device over there that appears to be waiting for us to approach it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it just Paimon, or does everything in this place seem just a little bit over-deliberate?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Well, it is the Holy Land, what did you expect...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, everything's so blatant... it's clearly begging to be noticed.

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: That's our Fischl for ya!

talks.objective: Enter the castle as the story unfolds
Enter the castle as the story unfolds
Find the source of the voice

dialogues.text: Someone, please, help me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, isn't this a statue?
Please don't refer to me like that! My name is Leon, and I am a knight of the Immernachtreich.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A knight? But you don't look like one...

dialogues.speaker: Leon
dialogues.text: You can't tell? Anyway, please don't speak ill of Sire Ozvaldo. He personally designed and distributed the armor for Die Nachtraben Ritter.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Sire Ozvaldo"?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, you must have heard that one before, surely? Oz's full name, "Ozvaldo Hrafnavins."

response.speaker: Xinyan
response.text: Oh... So "Megistus" was the easy pronunciation...

response.speaker: Leon
response.text: Dear friends, I apologize for interrupting your lovely conversation, but I believe you haven't been informed that the gate ahead has been locked.

response.speaker: Leon
response.text: I'm hoping you'll be kind enough to save me, and in exchange, I'll gladly teach you how to unlock the gate.

response.speaker: Mona
response.text: Well, I guess we'll have to save you then.

dialogues.speaker: Leon
dialogues.text: Valiant heroes... No words can express how grateful I feel right now. Thank you very much.

dialogues.speaker: Leon
dialogues.text: Remember, this is the password that unlocks the gate. "May my people be freed from the shackles of ancient decrees."

talks.objective: Repair the path to the tower
Head to the top of the tower

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like it's a dead end ahead. There's only a book.

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: Do you think what we just heard is the story from the book?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: So the "Holy Land" in the book's title refers to the Immernachtreich. This book sings the praises of the Prinzessin from the perspective of the people in her kingdom.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I guess this is kind of an autobiography...

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: We're on the last page of the book, but the story doesn't seem to have ended.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happens next? Paimon wants to know what happens next!

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: I guess we'll have to keep exploring. As for this book... wait, I have an idea... Now that we've finished it, let's close it.

talks.objective: Listen to the voices inside the room

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Huh? We've been transported again, but we're not back on the beach.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We are somewhere in... Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Greetings, Honorable Kaiserin der Verurteilung.
Amy, dear, I've made Steak and Fisherman's Toast. Come on, eat up before they go cold.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Ahem! Mother...
Oh, look at me, being so forgetful. Ahem! Dost thou knowest, Prinzessin der Verurteilung, that the hour of luncheon encroaches?

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Of course, Mother.

Ah, behold the view from the window, a delight to the senses! Prinzessin, Kaiserin, would you care to join the Kaiser der Verurteilung for a grand royal picnic? We shall enjoy the scenic view and partake of the delicacies granted to us by the heavens.

dialogues.speaker: Fischl
dialogues.text: Yes, I shall gladly join you!

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: Uh... does anyone wanna say anything about that?

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: Okay, I'll bite. So "Amy"... that's Fischl's real name?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like it. The other two voices were probably her mom and dad.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: ...Why are all of you giving me that look!?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Forgive me if this comes across as rude, but... is your surname truly Megistus?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Hmph, you think I was bluffing? My full title is and always has been "Mona Megistus, the Astrologist."

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: ...My apologies.

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: Don't you think that's a bit long?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Well, it's a special case. Only geniuses get titles like this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that makes no sense...

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: What are your thoughts on the scenes we just witnessed?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Well, it seems that "closing the book" is one way of affecting change in this mirage.

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: Well, I think it's sweet that Fischl's parents are willing to play along with her.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: They probably didn't indulge her forever. Based on the voice, this was surely a memory from her childhood? It's a different story now she's grown up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know a lot about Fischl, Mona!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: After all, we've been friends for quite a while.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Speaking of...I wonder where Fischl is now?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: That voice mentioned that she was heading out. We may as well go outside, and see if we can find anything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, we're back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, why are we back? We haven't finished the story yet!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: This feels as awful as purchasing a counterfeit astrology tutorial, or realizing you've forgotten your wallet in the middle of dinner...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ARGH!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Argh! This is torture!

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: I think they're a little bit upset.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: To be honest, I also don't like to read books that end on an unexpected cliffhanger.

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: Haha, no one likes that. Alright, let's enter the mirage again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good idea! Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: We're still here, it's not working

dialogues.speaker: Xinyan
dialogues.text: That's odd. We were able to enter earlier, but now, we can't.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Why!? Why are we being denied the opportunity to finish the book!? This is pure sadism!

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Hmm... Maybe it's because we've already reached the end of this book.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Before leaving the mirage, we saw that the book had been flipped to the final page. I believe "Hymn of the Holy Land" is divided into multiple volumes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's like one of those sneaky light novel marketing schemes... "If you want to know what happens next, please buy the next volume." Yuck.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Hmph! I have to see the ending.
Oh, oh, yes, the ending. Everyone wants to see how the books ends.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Huh? Who's there?
Oh, oh, heavens above, she saw me. Stand up straight, stand up straight.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: You're...
I'm "Ask-Me-For-Directions Arnold".

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That name's a little on the nose!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: So, Arnold, let me ask you something...

dialogues.speaker: Arnold
dialogues.text: It's "Ask-Me-For-Directions Arnold"!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: ...So, Ask-Me-For-Directions Arnold, let me ask you something!

dialogues.speaker: Arnold
dialogues.text: Yes, Ma'am!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Are there other volumes of "Hymn of the Holy Land"? Where can I find them?

dialogues.speaker: Arnold
dialogues.text: Oh, oh, you're asking the right person. "Hymn of the Holy Land" is the sacred scripture of the Immernachtreich. There are three volumes in total, with the other two stored in two high locations in the castle.

dialogues.speaker: Arnold
dialogues.text: If you wish to find the second volume, you must climb to the very top floor of the tower.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Tower? You mean, that tower over there?

dialogues.speaker: Arnold
dialogues.text: That is, indeed, the tower where the sacred scripture is stored. If you look closely to the cave right over there, you'll find a secret passage that will swiftly take you to the tower.

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Okay, thank you, Arnold.

dialogues.speaker: Arnold
dialogues.text: It's "Ask-Me-For-Directions Arnold"!

dialogues.speaker: Arnold
dialogues.text: Do you have any other questions for me, fair maiden? Concerning, perhaps, my relationship status, or monthly income...?

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: No! Goodbye!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Let's ignore that raven and proceed! There's a secret passage in the cave ahead that leads directly to the top of the tower.

dialogues.speaker: Arnold
dialogues.text: Oh, oh, but Ma'am! Are you sure you're not interested in me? I only shared with you the secrets of the Immernachtreich because of your great beauty! Ma'am! Wait...!

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: "The people celebrated and worshiped the Prinzessin's authority, and followed her call to migrate to the sacred land that would eventually be known as the Immernachtreich."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It really is the Immernachtreich!

dialogues.speaker: Mona
dialogues.text: Mm, it really looks the part... I'm quite impressed.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: "We established a nation on the Holy Land, revered the Prinzessin as The Absolute One, and introduced poetry, theater, and adventure to the Kingdom, laying the groundwork for the Immernachtreich."
